programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the historic border town of Chepstow, where medieval streets, independent shops and a strong charity shop scene set the stage for another fast-paced thrifting showdown. With its famous castle overlooking the River Wye, the town provides a dramatic backdrop for a race where sharp instincts and bold decisions could make all the difference.
Taking on the challenge are friends Ella and Issy, who are competing to raise money for their chosen charities. Armed with £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they are paired with expert thrifters, husband and husband Tom and Terry, and sent out across Chepstow’s charity shops in search of hidden gems that can be turned into profit.
Ella opts for a cautious but considered approach, hunting for quality homeware, collectibles and classic fashion pieces with reliable resale appeal. Early finds boost her confidence, including elegant glassware and vintage decorative items that promise steady returns. Issy, meanwhile, embraces a bolder strategy, gravitating towards statement furniture and eye-catching fashion – pieces that could either soar at auction or fall flat.
As the clock ticks down, tensions rise. A risky spend threatens to blow the budget, and both teams face tough calls about when to stop browsing and commit. Joanna keeps the pressure on, reminding them that hesitation can be just as costly as a bad buy.
Each contestant then chooses one item to be transformed. Rachel’s understated furniture find is refreshed into a stylish, contemporary piece, while Cerys’s more daring choice is given a dramatic makeover by a specialist upcycler, elevating it from charity shop cast-off to standout showpiece.
The episode builds to a live-streamed auction, where Ella and Issy must sell their collections to an online audience in real time. Nerves are high as bids come in thick and fast, and the balance of power shifts repeatedly. Strong storytelling and confident pitching prove crucial, while one surprise result sends shock waves through the competition.
When the final figures are revealed, there is a clear winner on the scoreboard. But the real triumph is the money raised for charity, proving once again that second-hand shopping can deliver real-world impact.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.sub-title: Can blue dye make me smarter ║ S1E5/6
programme.desc:
Stacey explores a trend that has racked up over 200 million online views worldwide - the use of methylene blue. It’s a textile dye that influencers claim can boost your brain power and gained worldwide notoriety when US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr appeared to put drops of it in his drink.
Stacey and Drs Alex and Nighat decide to do their own playful test to find out if it might work or if any perceived boost is better explained by the placebo effect. Intrigued by the origins of the trend, Stacey follows a digital trail that leads her to Cambridge University and 40 years of laboratory research that might, incredibly, see meth blue to be the inspiration for a new Alzheimer’s treatment.
Back at the hub, Stacey shocks the doctors with online deepfakes created to get them to promote new trends and supplements to unsuspecting followers. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
Danny Sebastian puts his best foot forward on the show when he visits Northamptonshire, a county with a long reputation for creating high-quality footwear. At the Museum of Leathercraft in Northampton, he delves into their collection of 10,000 items from around the world, from 3,000 years ago to the present day.
Curator James Hawksley shows Danny a sedan chair from the 1750s, a leather pigeon harness used to carry blood samples and two leather jugs called bombards because of their resemblance to the old bombard cannon. James even turns the table on Danny and reveals a mystery object for him to guess.
Across the county, two teams do battle in the historic village of Naseby. Expert David Harper heads up the red team, husband and wife Matt and Sunita, while the blues – father and son Surinder and Sukhip – are guided by Kate Bliss.
After a speedy start, the reds seem very relaxed… Can David focus their attention and help them to start spending? Over with the blues, a reproduction GR post box catches Surinder’s attention, but Kate isn’t convinced that it will deliver a profit.
In Stratford-upon-Avon, Danny asks auctioneer Mark Ashley for his estimates on the teams’ purchases but, as always, it comes down to how deep the bidders’ pockets are. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the elegant spa town of Harrogate, the gateway to the Yorkshire Dales, for a high-stakes thrifting showdown.
Today’s competitors are best friends – and former Traitors stars – Sonja and Aubrey, swapping the round table for the rails as they compete to raise money for a local cat sanctuary in Nottinghamshire. With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they split up with expert thrifters Jen and Mirain to tackle Harrogate’s 17 charity shops.
Sonja adopts a disciplined approach, focusing on timeless, high-quality fabrics and classic tailoring. She quickly snaps up a Viyella dress and a Harris Tweed jacket woven from 100 per cent Scottish wool – pieces she believes will always have an audience. But her laser focus on craftsmanship means she and Jen unknowingly pass up on Joanna’s pick of the day: a designer Manuel Ritz jacket with serious resale potential.
Across town, Aubrey leans into bold style and personality. His eye is drawn to standout 1980s fashion, including a pair of Paloma Picasso shoes that ooze retro glamour. However, Joanna worries he may be falling into a common thrifting trap – choosing pieces he loves personally rather than thinking purely about profit.
As time ticks away, attention turns to the all-important upcycling challenge. Aubrey takes a creative risk, pairing a floral embroidered tablecloth with a plain white shirt in the hope of creating a bespoke fashion statement. Meanwhile, Sonja opts for drama, gambling on a heavy Egyptian-style tapestry that could be transformed into a striking new piece.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must step into the spotlight as sellers. Aubrey’s natural charisma shines as he models his reworked creation, injecting energy and humour into the room. Sonja counters with calm authority, drawing on her knowledge of fabrics and tailoring to build bidder confidence.
When live sales are combined with a week of online trading, it’s an incredibly tight finish – proof that strategy, style and salesmanship all count in equal measure. But beyond the friendly rivalry, the real winner is Aubrey and Sonja's chosen charity, with a substantial total raised thanks to a fast-paced day of Yorkshire thrifting.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Abergavenny, known as Wales’s food capital and gateway to the Brecon Beacons, but will it also prove a gateway to profit?
Taking on the challenge are Port Talbot-born Luke and his partner from across the bridge in Bristol, Claudia, competing to raise money for the British Heart Foundation. This showdown pits the couple against each other, and their very different shopping instincts quickly come into play. Claudia admits she has no real plan, preferring safe, wearable fashion, while Luke arrives determined to beat her to the best finds before she even sees them.
Paired with expert thrifters Jen and Mirain, they’re given £100 each and just 60 minutes to tackle Abergavenny’s 13 charity shops. Luke dives straight in, snapping up a 1970s leather Collins writing case and later taking punts on a brass Japanese telescope and vintage Dandy comics. His boldest decision comes when Mirain persuades him to buy a second-hand wedding dress – a surprise gamble, but will it pay off and bring in a profit?
Meanwhile, Claudia and Jen stick to quality and timeless appeal, picking up a sheepskin jacket, a Jaeger pinafore dress and carefully chosen fashion pieces. But while Claudia feels confident with clothing, she is forced out of her comfort zone when it comes to upcycling, eventually securing a solid oak sideboard just before Luke can claim it.
This episode is shaped by chaos: torrential rain, mounting pressure and a dramatic last-minute sprint back to the very first shop of the day. With seconds to spare, Luke finally tries to buy his upcycle item – a £10 three-tier table he had walked away from almost an hour earlier – making this the most frantic finish yet.
At the live-streamed auction, Luke surprises everyone with confident pitching and detailed descriptions, pushing his profits higher than expected. Claudia, calmer and more natural on camera, charms bidders with warmth and humour, though her restored sideboard only breaks even.
Full of relationship-fuelled rivalry, wet weather drama and last-gasp decisions, this is one of the most unpredictable episodes yet, proving that hesitation can be just as risky as taking a gamble.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Arriving first at the barn is Pernilla de Bellis from Glasgow, carrying her family’s 1869 edition of Dante’s Divine Comedy. Once owned by her great-great-great-grandfather Giuseppe Fermini, the book became a cherished link to her beloved grandmother Nonna Carla, who used it to teach Pernilla to read and to appreciate literature. After Carla’s passing during the Covid-19 pandemic, the book became one of the few physical connections Pernilla still has to her. Fragile, torn and falling apart, the volume is entrusted to bookbinder Chris Shaw, who dismantles the book, repairs damaged pages, strengthens delaminated boards and carefully remounts the curved spine using his 'mummification' technique. Finally, he blends the worn cover with watercolours, restoring both strength and dignity to a treasured family heirloom.
Next to arrive is Mikey Akers from Coventry, accompanied by his mum, Louisa. Mikey received the Pride of Birmingham award aged 16 for his work raising awareness of verbal dyspraxia, a neurological speech disorder he has lived with since childhood. His poem I Am the Boy became the foundation of his advocacy, helping others understand the challenges he faced. Years later, Louisa accidentally knocked the award from a shelf, shattering the angel statuette. Ceramics expert Kirsten takes on the delicate reconstruction, navigating glossy resin surfaces, missing fragments and fragile joins. She rebuilds the wings, fills losses with soft wood filler and experiments with layered hand painting to recreate the award’s pristine, opaque white finish.
The third repair belongs to Justina Sebag-Montefiore from Cornwall, who brings her grandfather Michael’s handmade tsymbaly, a Ukrainian stringed instrument. Michael, known to Justina as Dido Mikeilo, grew up in the Carpathian Mountains before being taken to a work camp in Germany during World War II. After liberation, he settled in England, bringing with him a love of Ukrainian folk music. Unable to bring his original instrument from Ukraine, he built a new tsymbaly using postwar materials, carving wood with the skill of his mountain community. After decades of storage, the instrument is now loose, damaged and painfully out of tune.

As a historian, are you really jealous?' programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the sunny seaside resort of Eastbourne – often dubbed the charity shop capital of the UK – for a sibling showdown with serious heart behind it.
Competing today are brother and sister David and Theresa, raising money for DKMS in memory of a close friend. With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they team up with expert thrifters Pete and Lola to scour Eastbourne’s packed high street for hidden treasures.
Theresa is drawn to items with a story. She takes an early gamble on a vintage Presto briefcase and a rare Matchbox watch, hoping their character and nostalgia will resonate with bidders. As the clock ticks down, she finds herself in a frantic race to spend the remainder of her budget, leading to a chaotic finish that leaves her wondering if she’s done enough.
David, meanwhile, adopts a broader strategy, mixing high-end fashion with solid resale staples. He spots designer Helmut Lang jeans and a vintage GAP down jacket, balancing style with recognisable labels. In a dramatic moment, he also manages to secure Joanna’s pick of the day – a set of Queen Anne style nesting tables – right from under his sister’s nose, adding fuel to the sibling rivalry.
For the upcycling challenge, their visions couldn’t be more different. Theresa opts for bold, sustainable fashion, transforming a blazer and floral dress into a bespoke three-piece ensemble. David takes a more traditional route, sending his nesting tables for a careful French polish restoration designed to enhance the natural wood grain and period charm.
At the live-streamed auction, tensions run high. David leans into showmanship, bringing humour and flair to his pitches – even finding unexpected success with a retro DVD box set. Theresa counters with confident, composed selling, particularly when showcasing her fashion finds and creative upcycle.
When live and online sales are combined, the result is incredibly tight – proof that every decision, and every detail, counts. But beyond the sibling rivalry, the real triumph is the substantial sum raised for DKMS, turning a sunny day of seaside thrifting into something truly meaningful.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Arriving first at the barn is Pernilla de Bellis from Glasgow, carrying her family’s 1869 edition of Dante’s Divine Comedy. Once owned by her great-great-great-grandfather Giuseppe Fermini, the book became a cherished link to her beloved grandmother Nonna Carla, who used it to teach Pernilla to read and to appreciate literature. After Carla’s passing during the Covid-19 pandemic, the book became one of the few physical connections Pernilla still has to her. Fragile, torn and falling apart, the volume is entrusted to bookbinder Chris Shaw, who dismantles the book, repairs damaged pages, strengthens delaminated boards and carefully remounts the curved spine using his 'mummification' technique. Finally, he blends the worn cover with watercolours, restoring both strength and dignity to a treasured family heirloom.
Next to arrive is Mikey Akers from Coventry, accompanied by his mum, Louisa. Mikey received the Pride of Birmingham award aged 16 for his work raising awareness of verbal dyspraxia, a neurological speech disorder he has lived with since childhood. His poem I Am the Boy became the foundation of his advocacy, helping others understand the challenges he faced. Years later, Louisa accidentally knocked the award from a shelf, shattering the angel statuette. Ceramics expert Kirsten takes on the delicate reconstruction, navigating glossy resin surfaces, missing fragments and fragile joins. She rebuilds the wings, fills losses with soft wood filler and experiments with layered hand painting to recreate the award’s pristine, opaque white finish.
The third repair belongs to Justina Sebag-Montefiore from Cornwall, who brings her grandfather Michael’s handmade tsymbaly, a Ukrainian stringed instrument. Michael, known to Justina as Dido Mikeilo, grew up in the Carpathian Mountains before being taken to a work camp in Germany during World War II. After liberation, he settled in England, bringing with him a love of Ukrainian folk music. Unable to bring his original instrument from Ukraine, he built a new tsymbaly using postwar materials, carving wood with the skill of his mountain community. After decades of storage, the instrument is now loose, damaged and painfully out of tune.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
While the teams get into the rhythm of their shopping, host Danny Sebastian indulges one of his passions at an exhibition in London. The Music Is Black: A British Story celebrates 125 years of the influence of black music on culture and communities. At the V&A East Museum, Danny tours the exhibition with curator Jacqueline Springer, looking at a vinyl record with the words ‘Race Records’ on the sleeve, a label designed to segregate black music from white artists. There’s a piano belonging to the first black artist to have a UK number one single, Winifred Attwell, engraved with the names of her fans, a dress worn by Dame Shirley Bassey at the 2013 Academy Awards and a Banksy-designed vest worn by Stormzy at Glastonbury in 2019.
Hoping to turn their items into auction hits are dad and daughter Erike and Melissa, and mum and daughter Angela and Katie. With hundreds of stalls to choose from, the teams go in search of profitable antiques with their experts, Irita Marriott and Jonathan Pratt.
While the red team sizes up a vintage measuring tape, the blues check out a crackle-glazed pig sculpture. Then it’s off to auction in Bourne End, Buckinghamshire, to try to sell their buys to the highest bidders. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
Ex-con Joe Ruby is a volunteer at a local priory, tending to the grounds, seeking forgiveness and attempting to start a new life, all under the kind but watchful eye of Father David.
But when the body of one of the monks is found hastily buried in a remote part of the priory grounds, Oxford-educated DI Rose O’Connell and her green second in command, DS Raj Singh, are sent to investigate.
The mysterious circumstances make it a tricky case to solve. What secrets are these sacred grounds hiding? And what do these God-fearing suspects know about the murder? There’s Brother Christopher, the gentle monk who loves to garden, Sister Marie, the stern but kindly nun who runs Bible class and Father David, the cryptic, ever-wise prior. Alongside them is the victim’s brother Benedict, who is someone in need of support and money. And then there’s Joe himself, who with his criminal past becomes suspect number one for Rose and Raj.
But when Joe comes up with some insights from his own dodgy history, Rose senses that he may prove useful after all.
Finding themselves investigating alongside each other, Joe and Rose set out to solve the mystery of who killed Brother Mark, frustrating each other at every turn, only to uncover a truth far more shocking than either anticipated. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the historic border town of Chepstow, where medieval streets, independent shops and a strong charity shop scene set the stage for another fast-paced thrifting showdown. With its famous castle overlooking the River Wye, the town provides a dramatic backdrop for a race where sharp instincts and bold decisions could make all the difference.
Taking on the challenge are friends Ella and Issy, who are competing to raise money for their chosen charities. Armed with £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they are paired with expert thrifters, husband and husband Tom and Terry, and sent out across Chepstow’s charity shops in search of hidden gems that can be turned into profit.
Ella opts for a cautious but considered approach, hunting for quality homeware, collectibles and classic fashion pieces with reliable resale appeal. Early finds boost her confidence, including elegant glassware and vintage decorative items that promise steady returns. Issy, meanwhile, embraces a bolder strategy, gravitating towards statement furniture and eye-catching fashion – pieces that could either soar at auction or fall flat.
As the clock ticks down, tensions rise. A risky spend threatens to blow the budget, and both teams face tough calls about when to stop browsing and commit. Joanna keeps the pressure on, reminding them that hesitation can be just as costly as a bad buy.
Each contestant then chooses one item to be transformed. Rachel’s understated furniture find is refreshed into a stylish, contemporary piece, while Cerys’s more daring choice is given a dramatic makeover by a specialist upcycler, elevating it from charity shop cast-off to standout showpiece.
The episode builds to a live-streamed auction, where Ella and Issy must sell their collections to an online audience in real time. Nerves are high as bids come in thick and fast, and the balance of power shifts repeatedly. Strong storytelling and confident pitching prove crucial, while one surprise result sends shock waves through the competition.
When the final figures are revealed, there is a clear winner on the scoreboard. But the real triumph is the money raised for charity, proving once again that second-hand shopping can deliver real-world impact.

programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the elegant spa town of Harrogate, the gateway to the Yorkshire Dales, for a high-stakes thrifting showdown.
Today’s competitors are best friends – and former Traitors stars – Sonja and Aubrey, swapping the round table for the rails as they compete to raise money for a local cat sanctuary in Nottinghamshire. With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they split up with expert thrifters Jen and Mirain to tackle Harrogate’s 17 charity shops.
Sonja adopts a disciplined approach, focusing on timeless, high-quality fabrics and classic tailoring. She quickly snaps up a Viyella dress and a Harris Tweed jacket woven from 100 per cent Scottish wool – pieces she believes will always have an audience. But her laser focus on craftsmanship means she and Jen unknowingly pass up on Joanna’s pick of the day: a designer Manuel Ritz jacket with serious resale potential.
Across town, Aubrey leans into bold style and personality. His eye is drawn to standout 1980s fashion, including a pair of Paloma Picasso shoes that ooze retro glamour. However, Joanna worries he may be falling into a common thrifting trap – choosing pieces he loves personally rather than thinking purely about profit.
As time ticks away, attention turns to the all-important upcycling challenge. Aubrey takes a creative risk, pairing a floral embroidered tablecloth with a plain white shirt in the hope of creating a bespoke fashion statement. Meanwhile, Sonja opts for drama, gambling on a heavy Egyptian-style tapestry that could be transformed into a striking new piece.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must step into the spotlight as sellers. Aubrey’s natural charisma shines as he models his reworked creation, injecting energy and humour into the room. Sonja counters with calm authority, drawing on her knowledge of fabrics and tailoring to build bidder confidence.
When live sales are combined with a week of online trading, it’s an incredibly tight finish – proof that strategy, style and salesmanship all count in equal measure. But beyond the friendly rivalry, the real winner is Aubrey and Sonja's chosen charity, with a substantial total raised thanks to a fast-paced day of Yorkshire thrifting.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Abergavenny, known as Wales’s food capital and gateway to the Brecon Beacons, but will it also prove a gateway to profit?
Taking on the challenge are Port Talbot-born Luke and his partner from across the bridge in Bristol, Claudia, competing to raise money for the British Heart Foundation. This showdown pits the couple against each other, and their very different shopping instincts quickly come into play. Claudia admits she has no real plan, preferring safe, wearable fashion, while Luke arrives determined to beat her to the best finds before she even sees them.
Paired with expert thrifters Jen and Mirain, they’re given £100 each and just 60 minutes to tackle Abergavenny’s 13 charity shops. Luke dives straight in, snapping up a 1970s leather Collins writing case and later taking punts on a brass Japanese telescope and vintage Dandy comics. His boldest decision comes when Mirain persuades him to buy a second-hand wedding dress – a surprise gamble, but will it pay off and bring in a profit?
Meanwhile, Claudia and Jen stick to quality and timeless appeal, picking up a sheepskin jacket, a Jaeger pinafore dress and carefully chosen fashion pieces. But while Claudia feels confident with clothing, she is forced out of her comfort zone when it comes to upcycling, eventually securing a solid oak sideboard just before Luke can claim it.
This episode is shaped by chaos: torrential rain, mounting pressure and a dramatic last-minute sprint back to the very first shop of the day. With seconds to spare, Luke finally tries to buy his upcycle item – a £10 three-tier table he had walked away from almost an hour earlier – making this the most frantic finish yet.
At the live-streamed auction, Luke surprises everyone with confident pitching and detailed descriptions, pushing his profits higher than expected. Claudia, calmer and more natural on camera, charms bidders with warmth and humour, though her restored sideboard only breaks even.
Full of relationship-fuelled rivalry, wet weather drama and last-gasp decisions, this is one of the most unpredictable episodes yet, proving that hesitation can be just as risky as taking a gamble.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Arriving first at the barn is Pernilla de Bellis from Glasgow, carrying her family’s 1869 edition of Dante’s Divine Comedy. Once owned by her great-great-great-grandfather Giuseppe Fermini, the book became a cherished link to her beloved grandmother Nonna Carla, who used it to teach Pernilla to read and to appreciate literature. After Carla’s passing during the Covid-19 pandemic, the book became one of the few physical connections Pernilla still has to her. Fragile, torn and falling apart, the volume is entrusted to bookbinder Chris Shaw, who dismantles the book, repairs damaged pages, strengthens delaminated boards and carefully remounts the curved spine using his 'mummification' technique. Finally, he blends the worn cover with watercolours, restoring both strength and dignity to a treasured family heirloom.
Next to arrive is Mikey Akers from Coventry, accompanied by his mum, Louisa. Mikey received the Pride of Birmingham award aged 16 for his work raising awareness of verbal dyspraxia, a neurological speech disorder he has lived with since childhood. His poem I Am the Boy became the foundation of his advocacy, helping others understand the challenges he faced. Years later, Louisa accidentally knocked the award from a shelf, shattering the angel statuette. Ceramics expert Kirsten takes on the delicate reconstruction, navigating glossy resin surfaces, missing fragments and fragile joins. She rebuilds the wings, fills losses with soft wood filler and experiments with layered hand painting to recreate the award’s pristine, opaque white finish.
The third repair belongs to Justina Sebag-Montefiore from Cornwall, who brings her grandfather Michael’s handmade tsymbaly, a Ukrainian stringed instrument. Michael, known to Justina as Dido Mikeilo, grew up in the Carpathian Mountains before being taken to a work camp in Germany during World War II. After liberation, he settled in England, bringing with him a love of Ukrainian folk music. Unable to bring his original instrument from Ukraine, he built a new tsymbaly using postwar materials, carving wood with the skill of his mountain community. After decades of storage, the instrument is now loose, damaged and painfully out of tune.

As a historian, are you really jealous?' programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the sunny seaside resort of Eastbourne – often dubbed the charity shop capital of the UK – for a sibling showdown with serious heart behind it.
Competing today are brother and sister David and Theresa, raising money for DKMS in memory of a close friend. With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they team up with expert thrifters Pete and Lola to scour Eastbourne’s packed high street for hidden treasures.
Theresa is drawn to items with a story. She takes an early gamble on a vintage Presto briefcase and a rare Matchbox watch, hoping their character and nostalgia will resonate with bidders. As the clock ticks down, she finds herself in a frantic race to spend the remainder of her budget, leading to a chaotic finish that leaves her wondering if she’s done enough.
David, meanwhile, adopts a broader strategy, mixing high-end fashion with solid resale staples. He spots designer Helmut Lang jeans and a vintage GAP down jacket, balancing style with recognisable labels. In a dramatic moment, he also manages to secure Joanna’s pick of the day – a set of Queen Anne style nesting tables – right from under his sister’s nose, adding fuel to the sibling rivalry.
For the upcycling challenge, their visions couldn’t be more different. Theresa opts for bold, sustainable fashion, transforming a blazer and floral dress into a bespoke three-piece ensemble. David takes a more traditional route, sending his nesting tables for a careful French polish restoration designed to enhance the natural wood grain and period charm.
At the live-streamed auction, tensions run high. David leans into showmanship, bringing humour and flair to his pitches – even finding unexpected success with a retro DVD box set. Theresa counters with confident, composed selling, particularly when showcasing her fashion finds and creative upcycle.
When live and online sales are combined, the result is incredibly tight – proof that every decision, and every detail, counts. But beyond the sibling rivalry, the real triumph is the substantial sum raised for DKMS, turning a sunny day of seaside thrifting into something truly meaningful.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Arriving first at the barn is Pernilla de Bellis from Glasgow, carrying her family’s 1869 edition of Dante’s Divine Comedy. Once owned by her great-great-great-grandfather Giuseppe Fermini, the book became a cherished link to her beloved grandmother Nonna Carla, who used it to teach Pernilla to read and to appreciate literature. After Carla’s passing during the Covid-19 pandemic, the book became one of the few physical connections Pernilla still has to her. Fragile, torn and falling apart, the volume is entrusted to bookbinder Chris Shaw, who dismantles the book, repairs damaged pages, strengthens delaminated boards and carefully remounts the curved spine using his 'mummification' technique. Finally, he blends the worn cover with watercolours, restoring both strength and dignity to a treasured family heirloom.
Next to arrive is Mikey Akers from Coventry, accompanied by his mum, Louisa. Mikey received the Pride of Birmingham award aged 16 for his work raising awareness of verbal dyspraxia, a neurological speech disorder he has lived with since childhood. His poem I Am the Boy became the foundation of his advocacy, helping others understand the challenges he faced. Years later, Louisa accidentally knocked the award from a shelf, shattering the angel statuette. Ceramics expert Kirsten takes on the delicate reconstruction, navigating glossy resin surfaces, missing fragments and fragile joins. She rebuilds the wings, fills losses with soft wood filler and experiments with layered hand painting to recreate the award’s pristine, opaque white finish.
The third repair belongs to Justina Sebag-Montefiore from Cornwall, who brings her grandfather Michael’s handmade tsymbaly, a Ukrainian stringed instrument. Michael, known to Justina as Dido Mikeilo, grew up in the Carpathian Mountains before being taken to a work camp in Germany during World War II. After liberation, he settled in England, bringing with him a love of Ukrainian folk music. Unable to bring his original instrument from Ukraine, he built a new tsymbaly using postwar materials, carving wood with the skill of his mountain community. After decades of storage, the instrument is now loose, damaged and painfully out of tune.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
While the teams get into the rhythm of their shopping, host Danny Sebastian indulges one of his passions at an exhibition in London. The Music Is Black: A British Story celebrates 125 years of the influence of black music on culture and communities. At the V&A East Museum, Danny tours the exhibition with curator Jacqueline Springer, looking at a vinyl record with the words ‘Race Records’ on the sleeve, a label designed to segregate black music from white artists. There’s a piano belonging to the first black artist to have a UK number one single, Winifred Attwell, engraved with the names of her fans, a dress worn by Dame Shirley Bassey at the 2013 Academy Awards and a Banksy-designed vest worn by Stormzy at Glastonbury in 2019.
Hoping to turn their items into auction hits are dad and daughter Erike and Melissa, and mum and daughter Angela and Katie. With hundreds of stalls to choose from, the teams go in search of profitable antiques with their experts, Irita Marriott and Jonathan Pratt.
While the red team sizes up a vintage measuring tape, the blues check out a crackle-glazed pig sculpture. Then it’s off to auction in Bourne End, Buckinghamshire, to try to sell their buys to the highest bidders. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
Ex-con Joe Ruby is a volunteer at a local priory, tending to the grounds, seeking forgiveness and attempting to start a new life, all under the kind but watchful eye of Father David.
But when the body of one of the monks is found hastily buried in a remote part of the priory grounds, Oxford-educated DI Rose O’Connell and her green second in command, DS Raj Singh, are sent to investigate.
The mysterious circumstances make it a tricky case to solve. What secrets are these sacred grounds hiding? And what do these God-fearing suspects know about the murder? There’s Brother Christopher, the gentle monk who loves to garden, Sister Marie, the stern but kindly nun who runs Bible class and Father David, the cryptic, ever-wise prior. Alongside them is the victim’s brother Benedict, who is someone in need of support and money. And then there’s Joe himself, who with his criminal past becomes suspect number one for Rose and Raj.
But when Joe comes up with some insights from his own dodgy history, Rose senses that he may prove useful after all.
Finding themselves investigating alongside each other, Joe and Rose set out to solve the mystery of who killed Brother Mark, frustrating each other at every turn, only to uncover a truth far more shocking than either anticipated. After trying to go back in time, give back Tina for store credit and switching parents, he discovers that to be king, he needs people to reign over. programme.desc:

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc:
Ceòl is còmhradh bho cuirm shònraichte aig Celtic Connections a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de dh’òrain ùra Gàidhlig. A’ togail air pròiseact Òran Ùr bho BhBC Radio nan Gàidheal a bha a’ taisbeanadh òrain Gàidhlig a chaidh a dhèanamh bho thoiseach na linne, tha a’ chuirm ga chuir air dòigh le Gillebrìde MacIlleMhaoil, le ceòl bho rionnagan seinn na Gàidhlig. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Joy Dunlop.
Music and conversation from a special concert at Celtic Connections celebrating 25 years of new Gaelic songs. Building on BBC Radio nan Gàidheal’s Òran Ùr project that showcased Gaelic songs written since the turn of the century, the concert is curated by Gillebride MacMillan and features performances from stars of Gaelic song. Presented by Joy Dunlop.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc:
Tha Kate Nicleòid, maighdeann-mhara Innse Gall, gar toirt air turas gu cuid de na ceàrnaidhean àlainn nach eil cho aithnichte sna h-Eileanan an Iar agus bidh i a’ coinneachadh ri seanchaidhean le sgeulachdan iongantach mu na h-àiteachan air a bheil i gu math dèidheil, os cionn agus fon uisge.
Anns a’ cheathramh prògram, tha Kate a’ dèanamh air Beàrnaraigh na Hearadh agus a’ tachairt ri muinntir an àite, nam measg, Dòmhnall MacIllEathain a tha ag innse dhi mu dhòigh-beatha an àite sna làithean a dh’fhalbh, agus mu dheidhinn am fuamhaire ainmeil, Aonghas Mòr MacAsgaill, a rinn beòshlaint le cho àrd ’s a bha e – seachd troighean ’s naoi òirleach!
Tha i a’ cluinntinn sgeulachdan mu bheatha Ruairidh Sheathaich agus e na bhalach òg a’ fàs suas ann am Beàrnaraigh ’s a’ dol do dh’ àrd-sgoil sna Hearadh, am measg seanchas inntinneach mu chruth-tìre an eilein.
Tha i cuideachd a’ dèanamh oidhirp snàmh cuide ri na ròin agus bidh i ann an caidheag air a’ mhuir mu thimcheall An Tràigh Iar – an tràigh eireachdail a chaidh ainmeachadh bho chionn ghoirid mar an tràigh as bòidhche anns an Roinn Eòrpa.
Kate Macleod, The Hebridean Mermaid, takes us on a journey to some of the hidden gems of the Hebrides, meeting tradition bearers with remarkable stories about the places she loves to visit the most, above and below the water.
Kate makes her way to Berneray and meets locals such as Donald MacLean, who explains what life was like there in days gone by. He shares the story of Angus MacAskill, who made a living from his giant height - all seven foot, nine inches of him!
Roddy Shaw shares his story of growing up on Berneray and attending high school in Harris, as well as some interesting folklore about the landscape of the island. Kate attempts to swim with seals and also kayaks around the shores of the stunning West Beach, which was recently named the most beautiful beach in Europe.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Kate Macleod Executive Producer - Margaret Mary Murray Production Manager - Marion Maclean Producer - Peter Macqueen.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.sub-title: Ally, Soccer Is na Stàitean ║ S18
programme.desc:
Bho chladaichean nan Eilean Siar gu na solais deàlrach ann a Washington DC, tha Ally, Soccer Is Na Stàitean, ag innse mu dhreuchd ball-coise fear à Leòdhas, Ally ‘Bubble’ MacAoidh.
Le oideachadh air agus far an raon-cluiche ann am baile Phabail ann an Eilean Leòdhais, bha Ally na rionnag mhòr ball-coise is e dìreach na dheugaire.
Thàinig sgoilearachd shoirbheachail ann an Indiana anns na Stàitean Aonaichte an dèidh ùine còmhla ri Partick Thistle agus Ross County. Le dòchasan dreuchd proifeiseanta air fàire, bhris e a’ chas a chur às dhen amas a bh’ aige a bhith a’ cluich làn ùine.
A dh’ aindeoin am briseadh-cridhe, dh’ fhàs an gràdh a bh’ aig Ally airson a’ gheama agus cho dìcheallach ’s a bha e, agus chleachd e an cnap-starra seo mar spionnadh a bhith ag èirigh chun an ìre as àirde ann am ball-coise ann an dòigh eadar-dhealaichte.
An dèidh ùine ghoirid, chuidich obair na àidseant chluicheadairean e a bhith ag èirigh tron MLS, no Soccer a’ Phrìomh Lìog. Thug ùine na Leas-àrd-mhanaidsear, a’ cuideachadh ann a bhith a’ steidheachadh club ùr Nashville SC mar phrìomh sgioba anns an lìog, e gu bhith freagairt gairm bho DC United is e a’ gabhail obair na Àrd-mhanaidsear, agus b’ e aon den fheadhainn as òige ann an soccer Ameireaganach.
From the shores of the Hebrides to the bright lights of Washington DC, this documentary tells the footballing journey of Lewis man Ally ‘Bubble’ Mackay.
Schooled on and off the pitch in the village of Bayble on the Isle of Lewis, Ally was a teenage football prodigy. A successful football scholarship in Indiana in the USA followed spells with Partick Thistle and Ross County. With hopes of a professional career on the horizon, a devastating leg break shattered his dream of playing full time.
Despite the heartbreak, Ally's love for the game and determination only grew stronger, using his setback as motivation to find another way to the top flight of football. Soon a global career as a player agent set Ally up for a meteoric rise through MLS - or Major League Soccer. A spell as assistant general manager, helping establish new club Nashville SC as a major force in the league, led to the call from DC United to become one of the youngest general managers in American soccer.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: World Pipe Band Championships
programme.desc:
Tha Catrìona NicNèill air Lèanag Ghlaschu aig Farpais Chòmhlan Pìoba na Cruinne neo Na Worlds mar as fheàrr a dh’aithnichear iad. Thairis air a’ phrògram bidh i a’ toirt thugainn blasad den phìobaireachd ’s den drumaireachd as fheàrr bho air feadh an t-saoghail: à Alba, Èirinn, Èirinn a Tuath, Canada, Aimeireagaidh agus Sealainn Nuadh.
Bha 14 còmhlain a’ farpais aig Ìre a h-Aon am-bliadhna agus chì sibh na seallaidhean as fheàrr bhon dàrna latha. Bhuannaich Còmhlan Pìoba Inbhir Aora agus an Sgìre airson an dàrna turas sreath a chèile fo stiùir Màidsear na Pìoba Stuart Liddell MBE agus Prìomh Dhrumair a’ chòmhlain, Steven McWhirter. Cluinnear cuideachd ceòl bho chòmhlain eile, leithid Field Marshal Montgomery, Shotts agus Dykehead Caledonia agus Manawatu Scottish.
Carrie MacNeil introduces the bands competing at Grade One in the 2025 World Pipe Band Championships, better known as The Worlds. The show features the finest pipers and drummers from Scotland, Ireland, Northern Ireland, Canada and America.
In total, 14 bands competed across the two-day event on Glasgow Green. The programme features selected performances from the second day. Inveraray and District took home the title for the second consecutive year, under the direction of Pipe Major Stuart Liddell MBE and Lead Drummer, Steven McWhirter.
Also featured in the programme are performances from Field Marshal Montgomery, Shotts and Dykehead Caledonia and Manawatu Scottish.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc:
Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha Màiri Anna a’ siubhal le a caraid Ruairidh MacIlleathain air thòir air allt cho ainmeil sa th’ ann ann an dualchas nan Gàidheal – Allt an t-Siùcair aig Alasdair Mac Mhaighstir Alasdair, bàrd clìuteach na 18mh linn. Tha iad a’ coiseachd a-mach bho èirigh an uillt gu cladach feuch dè tha fhathast a’ fàs air na bruaichean an coimeas ri sealladh a’ bhàird air sgìre a bha beartach an nàdar. Agus tha Liusaidh a’ coimhead air aon dhe na rudan a tha nochdadh san dàn – na ròsan – agus mar a ghabhas an cleachdadh airson bidhe a tha math agus math dhuit.
Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke - The Wild Cooke -forage for nature’s bounty. Mary Ann travels with her friend Roddy MacLean in search of one of the most famous streams in Gaelic culture - the Sugar Brook that was celebrated by the 18th century poet Alexander MacDonald. They journey from source to shore to see what still grows there in comparison to the richness of nature described by the poet at the time. And Lucy looks at one of the elements celebrated in the poem - the roses - and how their fruit can be processed.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ dèanamh air New York airson a bhith na bean an taighe air a’ chiad Mhòd a bhios anns a’ bhaile. Leis gu bheil Seachdain Thartain New York air a bhith a’ dol airson còig bliadhna fichead, bidh Trusadh an làthair còmhla ri sliochd na h-Alba stèidhichte anns a’ bhaile ainmeil seo is iad a’ comharrachadh nan ceanglaichean eadar an dà dhùthaich. Bidh na mìltean de phìobairean agus dannsairean Gàidhealach ri fhaicinn air sràidean Mhanhattan agus am bliadhna seo tha seinneadairean Gàidhlig nam measg bho air feadh nan Stàitean Aonaichte agus Alba cuideachd.
Bidh sinn a’ leantainn Joy, An Comunn Gàidhealach agus sgioba na seachdaine Thartain ’s iad ag ullachadh airson a’ Mhòid – far am bi bùithtean obrach agus seiseanan cèilidh a’ gabhail àite. Bidh sinn cuideachd a’ coinneachadh ri caractaran inntinneach a tha gu bhith a’ gabhail pàirt san fharpais òrain Ghàidhlig seo – leithid Pamela Jean Agaloos à Queens a tha a’ seinn Òran Chaluim Sgàire làn faireachdainn is i air oideachadh fhaighinn bho Chairistìona Primrose! No John Grimaldi a tha ainmeil am measg Albannaich nan Stàitean agus a bhios a’ seinn ann an còmhlan de dh’ fhireannaich air a bheil an t-ainm Na h-Eileanaich (uill, tha e a’ fuireach ann an Eilean Mhanhattan, agus tha na seinneadairean eile a’ fuireach ann an Eilean Staton!) Tha cuid de na co-fharpaisich a’ siubhal à Utah, Virginia ’s Washington DC agus tha fiù ’s cuideigin à Glaschu a’ gabhail pàirt a’ riochdachadh na h-Alba!
Bidh BBC ALBA an sin airson an sgeulachd eachdraidheil seo ann an ceòl Gàidhlig a leantainn agus thathas an dòchas gum bi muinntir nam Mòdan agus daoine a tha taiceil don chànan sna Stàitean a’ frithealadh an tachartais seo san àm ri teachd! Tha a’ chiad neach a bhuannaicheas Mòd Seachdain Thartain New York gu bhith na rionnag ùr ann an saoghal na Gàidhlig ach an dùil cò an neach a bhios soirbheachail?
Joy Dunlop heads to New York City to host the first ever New York Mòd. programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ dèanamh air New York airson a bhith na bean an taighe air a’ chiad Mhòd a bhios anns a’ bhaile. Leis gu bheil Seachdain Thartain New York air a bhith a’ dol airson còig bliadhna fichead, bidh Trusadh an làthair còmhla ri sliochd na h-Alba stèidhichte anns a’ bhaile ainmeil seo is iad a’ comharrachadh nan ceanglaichean eadar an dà dhùthaich. Bidh na mìltean de phìobairean agus dannsairean Gàidhealach ri fhaicinn air sràidean Mhanhattan agus am bliadhna seo tha seinneadairean Gàidhlig nam measg bho air feadh nan Stàitean Aonaichte agus Alba cuideachd.
Bidh sinn a’ leantainn Joy, An Comunn Gàidhealach agus sgioba na seachdaine Thartain ’s iad ag ullachadh airson a’ Mhòid – far am bi bùithtean obrach agus seiseanan cèilidh a’ gabhail àite. Bidh sinn cuideachd a’ coinneachadh ri caractaran inntinneach a tha gu bhith a’ gabhail pàirt san fharpais òrain Ghàidhlig seo – leithid Pamela Jean Agaloos à Queens a tha a’ seinn Òran Chaluim Sgàire làn faireachdainn is i air oideachadh fhaighinn bho Chairistìona Primrose! No John Grimaldi a tha ainmeil am measg Albannaich nan Stàitean agus a bhios a’ seinn ann an còmhlan de dh’ fhireannaich air a bheil an t-ainm Na h-Eileanaich (uill, tha e a’ fuireach ann an Eilean Mhanhattan, agus tha na seinneadairean eile a’ fuireach ann an Eilean Staton!) Tha cuid de na co-fharpaisich a’ siubhal à Utah, Virginia ’s Washington DC agus tha fiù ’s cuideigin à Glaschu a’ gabhail pàirt a’ riochdachadh na h-Alba!
Bidh BBC ALBA an sin airson an sgeulachd eachdraidheil seo ann an ceòl Gàidhlig a leantainn agus thathas an dòchas gum bi muinntir nam Mòdan agus daoine a tha taiceil don chànan sna Stàitean a’ frithealadh an tachartais seo san àm ri teachd! Tha a’ chiad neach a bhuannaicheas Mòd Seachdain Thartain New York gu bhith na rionnag ùr ann an saoghal na Gàidhlig ach an dùil cò an neach a bhios soirbheachail?

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.sub-title: Ally, Soccer Is na Stàitean ║ S18
programme.desc:
Bho chladaichean nan Eilean Siar gu na solais deàlrach ann a Washington DC, tha Ally, Soccer Is Na Stàitean, ag innse mu dhreuchd ball-coise fear à Leòdhas, Ally ‘Bubble’ MacAoidh.
Le oideachadh air agus far an raon-cluiche ann am baile Phabail ann an Eilean Leòdhais, bha Ally na rionnag mhòr ball-coise is e dìreach na dheugaire.
Thàinig sgoilearachd shoirbheachail ann an Indiana anns na Stàitean Aonaichte an dèidh ùine còmhla ri Partick Thistle agus Ross County. Le dòchasan dreuchd proifeiseanta air fàire, bhris e a’ chas a chur às dhen amas a bh’ aige a bhith a’ cluich làn ùine.
A dh’ aindeoin am briseadh-cridhe, dh’ fhàs an gràdh a bh’ aig Ally airson a’ gheama agus cho dìcheallach ’s a bha e, agus chleachd e an cnap-starra seo mar spionnadh a bhith ag èirigh chun an ìre as àirde ann am ball-coise ann an dòigh eadar-dhealaichte.
An dèidh ùine ghoirid, chuidich obair na àidseant chluicheadairean e a bhith ag èirigh tron MLS, no Soccer a’ Phrìomh Lìog. Thug ùine na Leas-àrd-mhanaidsear, a’ cuideachadh ann a bhith a’ steidheachadh club ùr Nashville SC mar phrìomh sgioba anns an lìog, e gu bhith freagairt gairm bho DC United is e a’ gabhail obair na Àrd-mhanaidsear, agus b’ e aon den fheadhainn as òige ann an soccer Ameireaganach.
From the shores of the Hebrides to the bright lights of Washington DC, this documentary tells the footballing journey of Lewis man Ally ‘Bubble’ Mackay.
Schooled on and off the pitch in the village of Bayble on the Isle of Lewis, Ally was a teenage football prodigy. A successful football scholarship in Indiana in the USA followed spells with Partick Thistle and Ross County. With hopes of a professional career on the horizon, a devastating leg break shattered his dream of playing full time.
Despite the heartbreak, Ally's love for the game and determination only grew stronger, using his setback as motivation to find another way to the top flight of football. Soon a global career as a player agent set Ally up for a meteoric rise through MLS - or Major League Soccer. A spell as assistant general manager, helping establish new club Nashville SC as a major force in the league, led to the call from DC United to become one of the youngest general managers in American soccer.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre ’s i gar toirt tro cheumannan a bharrachd ann a bhith ag ionnsachadh na Gàidhlig. Bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean làitheil agus, mar thè a dh’ionnsaich na Gàidhlig i fhèin, bheir Joy mìneachadh dhuinn air briathrachas, gràmar is gnathasan-cainnte ann an dòigh a tha furasta a thuigsinn.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh a th’ air Gàidhlig ionnsachadh gu àrd ìre neo a thogadh leis a’ Ghàidhlig air falbh bho sgìrean traidiseanta na Gàidhealtachd, agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh dhuinn air annasan is cuspairean ’s e air chuairt air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot, ann am pod-chraolaidhean SpeakGaelic air BBC Sounds agus tha na prògraman air fad rin lorg le fo-thiotalan air sianal YouTube SpeakGaelic.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to keep on speaking Gaelic. As in previous series, she introduces and explains usage for words and phrases on everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through vocabulary, grammar and idiom on topics such as medicine, politics, community and exercise.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, and the intrepid Calum Maclean ventures to forgotten corners of Scotland seeking hidden treasures.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot, in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds and with English subtitles on SpeakGaelic’s YouTube channel. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Producer - Donald Macleod Executive Producer - Una McDonald.

A' tòiseachadh le prògram sònraichte a’ Mhòid bidh Màiri NicAonghais agus John Joe MacNèill a’ dol an aghaidh Joy Dunlop agus Art MacCarmaig airson airgead a bhuannachadh airson cathrannas. programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Air an 15mh dhen Ghiblean, 2019, sgrios teine mòr mullach Notre-Dame, a' leagail a saighead, a' briseadh a crùisle agus a' lagachadh a ballachan. Às dèidh bliadhna de dh'obair daingneachaidh, chaidh dà cheud luchd-saidheans dhan chathair-eaglais airson rannsachadh a dhèanamh air an togalach ainmeil seo far a bheil cùisean-iongnaidh is taisbeanaidhean fhathast rin lorg.
Dh'obraich àrc-eòlaichean, eachdraichean agus ailtirean còmhla air a' phròiseact gun shamhail seo: fad mhìosan, rinn iad sgrùdadh air a' chrùisle mheadhan-aoiseach a bh' air tuiteam. Fhad 's a bhathar a' cruinneachadh, a' seòrsachadh 's a' rannsachadh na blocaichean, lorg iad comharran snaidhte sa chloich a bh' air am falach roimhe. Cuimhneachain a dh'fhàg fir bho chionn còrr air ochd ceud bliadhna. An tèid aca air na boghachan is crùislean mheadhan-aoiseach a tha deatamach dha seasmhachd an togalaich ath-thogail?
Nì am film seo taisbeanadh air togail na cathair-eaglais iongantaich seo, a' dèanamh luaidh air comas a h-ailtirean 's a luchd-togail. A' cleachdadh bathar-bog 3D ùr aig a bheil comas gun shamhail, nì luchd-rannsachaidh oidhirp air fuasglaidhean fhaighinn air cùisean-iongnaidh Notre-Dame. An tèid aca air togalach a sheas troimh ochd linn chaochlaideach a chàradh?
On April 15, 2019, a huge fire consumed Notre-Dame’s roof, taking down its arrow, piercing its vaults and weakening the walls. After a year of consolidation work, 200 scientists entered the cathedral, aiming to study this world-renowned monument which holds a series of enigmas and revelations.
Archaeologists, historians and architects worked hand in hand on this unprecedented project: for months, they studied the cathedral's collapsed medieval arch. While collecting, organising and analysing every block, they discovered precious marks inscribed in the stone - until now hidden. The memory of gestures left by men more than 800 years ago. Will they be able to rebuild such medieval arches and vaults, key elements of the structure’s durability?
This film unveils the genesis of this tremendous cathedral, highlighting the mastery of its architects and builders. Thanks to new 3D software, researchers can work to solve Notre-Dame’s enigmas.

programme.title: Caileag nan Eun
programme.desc:

Nuair a smaoineachas sinn air a’ chur-seachad seo is mathaid nach e òigridh a’ chiad fheadhainn a thig a-steach oirnn - ach tha Caitlin airson seo atharrachadh. Mar sin, tha i a’ falbh air turas mòr mun cuairt Alba, a shireadh daoine òga aig a bheil an aon ùidh rithe fhèin. Anns a’ phrògram seo cluinnear na sgeulachdan pearsanta acasan mu na buannachdan agus mun mhòr-thlachd a tha iad a’ faighinn às a’ chur-seachad iongantach seo.

Keen to connect with people who share her passion, she sets off on a road trip around Scotland to meet other birders who are defying the typecasts and to uncover some of the personal stories behind the hobby. Together, they share the joys and frustrations of birdwatching as well as the pure exhilaration in spotting a bird that means so much to them.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc:

Thèid Coinneach MacFhraing a Chataibh gus feuchainn air ceann-uidhe a bheò-ghlac ginealaichean do shreapadairean, Bodach an Stòir. Feumaidh sìde, seòl na mara agus taic còmpanaich ùir uile tighinn ri chèile gus bàrr an staca aibheisich seo a ruighinn.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Coinneach Rankin Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod.

The puffin burrow has been flooded and May invites the little pufflings to come and stay with her until the mess is fixed. Although there's excitement and merriment at first, Baba soon becomes unsure about sleeping so far from home. Narrator - John Carmichael Oona - Zoe Drysdale Mama - Ellen Macdonald Papa - Calum Macaulay Baba - Adam Kaiess Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc:
A' dèanamh ceilidh-cadail air na Hoots, feumaidh Oona 's Baba gabhail ri cadal tron latha, mar na cailleachan-oidhch' bheag. Chan eil an gnothach cho furasta 's a bha iad an dùil ge-tà, gu h-àraidh dha Baba beag bochd!
When sleeping over with the Hoots, Oona and Baba realise that they must sleep during the day, just like their owl friends. However, the reality of getting to sleep in the middle of the day isn't so easy, especially for poor Baba. Narrator - John Carmichael Oona - Zoe Drysdale Mama - Ellen Macdonald Mossy - Lachlann Macleod Baba/Pop - Adam Kaiess Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec Macdonald.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc:
Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Leo is Dara agus Bòtannan, an cat eireachdail aca. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh cait agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Leo is Dara agus Bòtannan a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean.
Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together, they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home. In this episode, Eilidh visits Leo and Dara and their handsome cat Bòtannan. We find out how to look after cats and about all the lovely stuff Leo, Dara and Bòtannan get up to together.
Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home - including how best to handle, train and feed them. Presenter - Eilidh Cormack Producer - Donna Murchison Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:

programme.desc:
Bekah agus Zach leis a’ chuid as fheàrr bho na farpaisean ciùil dhan òigridh aig Mòd Ghlaschu. Cluinnidh sinn cuideachd bho chuid de na farpaisich a ghabh pàirt Diluain agus Dimàirt.
Bekah and Zach with highlights from the junior music competitions at this year’s Glasgow Mod. We also meet some of those who took part in Monday and Tuesday’s competitions.

Tha fear òg ùr air an eilean - bleigeard beag breugach. Nuair a tha è falbh le rothair Mharco, feumaidh an triùir a ghlacadh. Ach nach eil fhios gu bheil MacIomhair cuir a shròin a-steach!
When a new boy arrives on the island, Della, Lou and Marco are quick to work out that he’s a nasty piece of work. Of course he is, he’s MacIomhair’s nephew! Kyle is a little thief and a liar. When he steals Marco’s bike, the three hatch a plan to catch him. Will it work? And will MacIomhair ever say sorry? Gaelic comedy for young viewers. Tha mathair Hilda a’ miannachadh gun dèanadh i caraidean ùra ann an Trolberg. An àite sin, tha Hilda a’ coinneachadh fitheach a tha air a chuimhne a chall.
Hilda’s mother wishes that she could make new friends in Trolberg. Instead, Hilda meets a raven who has lost his memory. For a splendid accompaniment treat, Abigail makes tahini sesame cookies. Very tasty, packed with flavour and white chocolate!

programme.desc: Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Maighread Stiùbhart. Music and chat presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee with guest Margaret Stewart.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc:
Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history.
Murdo travels close to Stobo in the Scottish Borders to visit Dawyck Botanic Garden when the autumn colours are at their most vibrant. He also speaks to a mycologist about the garden’s Cryptogamic Sanctuary and why fungi is important in so many ways. Roddy Maclean talks about an autumn favourite - the bramble, and Dr Mark Newman from the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh tells us about how trees reproduce.
Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta, an làrach agus agus an eachdraidh.
Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’dol gu Gàrradh Luibheanach Dawyck, faisg air Stobo sna Crìochan, nuair is dealraiche a tha duilleach an fhoghair. Gheibh e facal air sàr eòlaiche air balgain-buachrach mu na seòrsaichean a tha glèidhte sa ghàrradh, agus dè tha gam fàgail cho cudromach ann an iomadh dòigh.Bruidhnidh Ruairidh MacIlleathain mu lus is toil leis fhèin as t-fhoghar – an smeur-dubh; agus innsidh an t-Oll. Mark Newman bho Ghàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn Èidinn dhuinn mu ghineadh chraobh.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Murdo Macdonald Producer - Julie McCrone Director - Shona Masson.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc:
Gregor MacLeod inherited his grannie’s old cookery book. She had written down over 50 recipes by hand and Gregor has set himself the challenge of cooking his way through them.
Gregor takes on grannie’s recipe for rhubarb and orange jam, using his own home-grown rhubarb. Her trifle recipe also catches Gregor’s eye but he can’t resist putting his own spin on it with amaretti biscuits.
Liver is perhaps not quite as fashionable these days but Gregor attempts grannie’s recipe for liver casserole. He talks to his neighbour, once the village butcher, about how commonly it was eaten and gives his verdict on the finished dish.
Gregor’s uncle hears there is baking going and calls in for a ceilidh to try Gregor’s oatcakes. He remembers his mother’s cooking well so if anyone’s going to know whether Gregor is doing her recipes justice – it’s him.
Fhuair Griogar MacLeòid seann leabhar còcaireachd a sheanmhair mar dhìleab: comhairle na làmh-sgrìobhaidh fhèin air còrr is lethcheud dinnear is greim blasta a dhèanamh. Tha Griogar a’ cur roimhe a’ dol tron a leabhar a’ feuchainn orra.
Sa phrògram seo nì e an t-sili a’ mhol i, le ruadhbhàrr is orainds. Tha e a’ feuchainn air an trifle aice cuideachd - ach cuiridh e a dhreach fhèin air, le briosgaidean amaretti.
‘S dòch’ nach eil grùthan uabhasach fasanta an-diugh, ach tha Griogar ga bhruich mar a bha granaidh a’ moladh. Cluinnidh e bho a nàbaidh, seann bhùidsear a’ bhaile, mu cho tric sa bhathar uairigin ga ithe, is bheir a nàbaidh dha a bheachd air an annlan.
Tha bràthair athar Ghriogar a’ tadhal a dh’fheuchainn aran-corca. Tha deagh chuimhne aigesan air còcaireachd a mhàthar - ma thuigeas duine an d’rinn Griogar am biadh cho math rithe, seo è.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Gregor Macleod Director - Ramsay MacMahon.

programme.title: Julie Fleeting
programme.desc:
Determined to play, nine-year-old Julie Fleeting’s life in football began with a local boys club. It was the first step in achieving a dream she didn’t even know existed. From playing professionally in America to winning multiple honours with Arsenal, and scoring more goals for Scotland than anyone else, Julie has consistently inspired, empowered and led from the front. In a story of tenacity and triumph, Julie’s journey in football is also one of family, humility and respect.
Thòisich Julie Fleeting a’ cluiche ball-coise còmhla ri sgioba bhalaich aig naoi bliadhna a dh’aois, a’ chiad cheum air an t-slighe gu dreuchd nach robh i fiù’s a smaointinn a bha comasach dhith. Bho bhith a’ cluiche gu proifeiseanta ann an Ameireagaidh gu togail dhuaisean aig Arsenal sa cur barrachd thadhail do dh’ Alba seach duine sam bith eile, tha Julie air a bhith na misneachd sna h-eisimpleir fad a beatha. Ach tha a slighe ann am ball-coise cuideachd mu dheidhinn theaghlach, irisleachd agus spèis.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Iona Ballantyne Director - Margot McCuaig Editor - Kenny Park Executive Producer - Iseabail Mactaggart Executive Producer - Calum McConnell.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc:
Tha Fiona NicChoinnich agus Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air Toby Lee gu Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House aig Belladrum 2025. Ged nach eil Toby ach 20 bliadhna a dh’aois, tha na sàr-sgilean cluiche agus a ghuth iongantach air cothroman fhuasgladh dha air an àrd-ùrlar leis an luchd-ciùil as fheàrr – mar Buddy Guy, Billy Gibbons, Peter Frampton, Slash agus Joe Bonamassa.
Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome Toby Lee to the Hot House Stage at Belladrum. A mind-blowing guitarist and a voice to match, the 20-year-old’s music belies his age and has seen him sharing the stage with the best in the business, including Buddy Guy, Billy Gibbons, Peter Frampton, Slash and Joe Bonamassa.

programme.title: Trail West is Caraidean aig Barrowland
programme.desc:
Cuirm shònraichte bhon Bharrowland Ballroom, le ceòl bho Trail West, Beinn Lee is Ruairidh Gray. A’ comharrachadh 15 bliadhna mar chòmhlan, thug Trail West cuireadh do an caraidean ceòlmhor gu ‘dachaigh rock & roll’ agus rinn an luchd-leantainn an slighe chun an talla-ciùil as cliùitiche ann an Glaschu airson a’ phàrtaidh as fheàrr air a’ Chost’ an Iar.
A special concert from the Barrowland Ballroom featuring performances from Trail West, Beinn Lee and Ruairidh Gray. Celebrating 15 years as a band, Trail West invited their musical pals to 'the home of rock and roll', so their fans descended on Glasgow’s most iconic venue for the ultimate west coast party.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Because they are a little short of money, and considering cash notes are only little papers with drawings on them, Petit and his friends decide to create their own money and buy anything they want. Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh a’ dol a chèilidh air Blor is tha e a’ sèideadh builgean mòr an urra dhaibh, airson is gun tèid acasan ri sgèith san adhar cuideachd. Tha iad a’ dol nas àirde is nas àirde is nas àirde, is tha an t-eagal air Àtaidh.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc:
Tha Sionnach a’ lorg dìsinn am measg stuth a chaidh a chaith gu aon taobh. Tha an dìsinn a’ còrdadh ri Comhachag agus tha e a’ dèanamh iomlaid air a shon leis an dèideag as fheàrr leis. Tha Sionnach air a dhòigh leis an dèideag ùr ach tha Comhachag ga h-ionndrainn gu mòr. Chan eil guth aig Sionnach air a toirt air ais gus an smaoinich Maigheach ghleusta air dòigh anns an toir i a’ chomhstrì gu ceann.
Fox finds a giant dice in a box of discarded belongings. Owl really likes it too and decides to trade it for his favourite doll, Oehoe. Fox enjoys life with his new toy, but Owl comes to realise he made a huge mistake; he misses Oehoe so much! Fox, however, won’t give it back. Hare thinks of a cunning way to solve the stand-off. programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc:
Tha a’ chiad teirm a’ tighinn gu crìch aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus tha e follaiseach a-nise gu bheil comhstrì eadar cuid den luchd-obrach. Tha Ms Sharpe agus cuid de na sgoilearan aice trang ag ullachadh airson a’ Mhòid, agus chan eil cùisean idir rèidh eadar Danny agus Mrs Fullerton.
As the first term comes to an end, it’s evident that tensions are building at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. Miss Sharpe and her pupils are busy preparing for the Mòd and it’s looking as if Danny and Mrs Fullerton are out for revenge.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc:
Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra...
Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead? Director - Donald Ewen MacKinnon Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod.

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc:
Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo tha i a’ sireadh an “slime” as fheàrr, ach saoil dè an reasabaidh a bhios soirbheachail? An e “slime” cruasbach, “slime” a ghabhas ithe, “slime” bith-chnàmhach no “slime” molach?
Choirstaidh is looking for the best slime recipe, but what will it be? Crunchy, edible, biodegradable or fluffy slime? Presenter - Chiorstaidh Macarthur Producer - Jamie Kieran.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:
Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc:
Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha Liusaidh a’ toirt Màiri Anna dhachaigh gu dùthaich a h-òige, Shropshire, far an do thòisich a beatha an co-bhuinn ri nàdar. Tha iad a’ trusadh bhalgan-buachair nach gabh a lorg an Gàidhealtachd na h-Alba, agus a’ dèanamh picil leotha. Tha iad a’ beachdachadh air àrainneachd gu math eadar-dhealaichte bho an dachaigh an Alba le taic bho athair Liusaidh, a’ tadhal air darach a tha co-dhiù 800 bliadhn’ a dh’aois, agus a’ trusadh eidheann-thalmhainn, lus cùbhraidh a tha càirdeach do phionnd is sèids. Agus tha an còmhnaidh ùine ann airson basgaid ùir.
Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke - The Wild Cooke -forage for nature’s bounty. Lucy takes Mary Ann to Shropshire where she grew up and began her life in harmony with nature. They collect fungi that can’t be found in Highland Scotland and pickle them. With some help from Lucy’s dad, they visit an 800-year-old oak tree and forage for ground ivy, a fragrant herb related to mint and sage. And there’s always time for a new basket.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc:
Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh.
The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Kirsty Macdonald Producer - Andy Mackinnon Production Manager - Eilidh Johnson Executive Producer - Margaret Cameron.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc:
Angus Mackay is joined by his daughter Ruth as they go to sea on a spectacular summer's day. Along the way they encounter a large pod of dolphins who take great delight in racing their small boat. Then it’s time for fishing and chat about the formative role of fishing in Ruth’s upbringing.
Anns an dàrna prògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha nighean Aonghais, Rut, còmhla ris agus iad aig muir air latha samhraidh eireachdail. Air an t-slighe, coinnichidh iad ri buidheann leumadairean-mara a tha dannsa mun eathar. Às dèidh sin, tha an t-àm ann airson iasgach agus còmhradh mun bhuaidh a bh’ aig iasgach air beatha Ruth.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Bodach an Stòir ║ Dàna. S3. ALBAE1/4. Old Man of Stoer ║ Dàna. S3. ALBAE1/4
programme.desc:

programme.title: Cù Leis Thu?
A Puppy for Padruig
programme.desc:
In this exciting final episode, Peter faces a big decision: which breed will he choose as his second puppy and companion for Flòraidh? So far, he’s met skye terriers, deerhounds, Dandie Dinmont terriers, westies and labradors: all with qualities that have won him over. But before he makes his choice, Peter has one more type of dog in mind: rescue dogs. With patience and love, rescue dogs can make wonderful pets - could one of them be the perfect match?
Peter visits friends with rescue and mixed-breed dogs, before travelling to Fife to meet top scent-detection dogs, all of whom began as rescues. Inspired by what he sees, Peter explores the rewarding companionship a rescue dog can bring. Finally, he heads to a local dog show, revisiting some of the remarkable breeds he’s encountered, before returning to the hut to make his heartfelt decision.
Anns a’ phrògram dheireannach thiamhaidh seo, tha co-dhùnadh mòr roimh Phàdruig: cò am briod a thaghas e airson a bhith na chompanach dha Flòraidh? Gu ruige seo choinnich e ri abhagan Sgitheanach, mialchoin-fhèidh, abhagan Dandie Dinmont, Westidhean agus Labradoran – agus bha iad uile tarraingeach. Ach mus dèan e co-dhùnadh, tha aire Phàdruig air seòrsa cù eile: coin theasairgte. Le foighidinn agus gaol, 's urrainn dha coin theasairgte a bhith nam peataichean air leth – saoil am biodh aon dhiubh freagarrach?
Tha Pàdruig a' tadhal air caraidean aig a bheil coin theasairgte agus gnèithean measgaichte, mus dèan e air Fìobha a choinneachadh ri coin sròinich – a thòisich nan coin theasairgte. Air a mhisneachadh leis na tha e a' faicinn, tha Pàdruig a' rannsachadh na buannachdan a thig an cois cù teasairgte. Mu dheireadh, thèid e gu fèill-chon ionadail, far am faic e cuid de na seòrsachan coin a choinnich e roimhe, mus till e dhan bhothag airson co-dhùnadh a dhèanamh.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Julie Fleeting
programme.desc:
Determined to play, nine-year-old Julie Fleeting’s life in football began with a local boys club. It was the first step in achieving a dream she didn’t even know existed. From playing professionally in America to winning multiple honours with Arsenal, and scoring more goals for Scotland than anyone else, Julie has consistently inspired, empowered and led from the front. In a story of tenacity and triumph, Julie’s journey in football is also one of family, humility and respect.
Thòisich Julie Fleeting a’ cluiche ball-coise còmhla ri sgioba bhalaich aig naoi bliadhna a dh’aois, a’ chiad cheum air an t-slighe gu dreuchd nach robh i fiù’s a smaointinn a bha comasach dhith. Bho bhith a’ cluiche gu proifeiseanta ann an Ameireagaidh gu togail dhuaisean aig Arsenal sa cur barrachd thadhail do dh’ Alba seach duine sam bith eile, tha Julie air a bhith na misneachd sna h-eisimpleir fad a beatha. Ach tha a slighe ann am ball-coise cuideachd mu dheidhinn theaghlach, irisleachd agus spèis.

programme.title: World Pipe Band Championships
programme.desc:
Tha Catrìona NicNèill air Lèanag Ghlaschu aig Farpais Chòmhlan Pìoba na Cruinne neo Na Worlds mar as fheàrr a dh’aithnichear iad. Thairis air a’ phrògram, bidh i a’ toirt thugainn blasad den phìobaireachd ’s den drumaireachd as fheàrr bho air feadh an t-saoghail: à Alba, Èirinn, Èirinn a Tuath, Canada agus Aimeireagaidh.
Bha 14 còmhlain a’ farpais aig Ìre a h-Aon am-bliadhna agus chì sibh na seallaidhean as fheàrr bhon dàrna latha. Bhuannaich Inbhir Aora agus an Sgìre airson an dàrna turas sreath a chèile agus iad fo stiùir Màidsear na Pìoba Stuart Liddell MBE agus Prìomh Dhrumair a’ chòmhlain, Steven McWhirter.
Cluinnear cuideachd ceòl bho Peoples Ford Boghall agus Bathgate Caledonia, St. Laurence O’Toole agus Na 78th Fraser Highlanders.
Carrie MacNeil introduces the bands competing at Grade One in the 2025 World Pipe Band Championships, better known as The Worlds. The show features the finest pipers and drummers from Scotland, Ireland, Northern Ireland, Canada and America.
In total 14 bands competed across the two-day event on Glasgow Green. The programme features selected performances from the climactic second day. Inveraray and District took home the title for the second consecutive year under the direction of Pipe Major Stuart Liddell MBE and Lead Drummer, Steven McWhirter.
Also featured in the programme are performances from Peoples Ford Boghall and Bathgate Caledonia, St. Laurence O’Toole and the 78th Fraser Highlanders.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the historic border town of Chepstow, where medieval streets, independent shops and a strong charity shop scene set the stage for another fast-paced thrifting showdown. With its famous castle overlooking the River Wye, the town provides a dramatic backdrop for a race where sharp instincts and bold decisions could make all the difference.
Taking on the challenge are friends Ella and Issy, who are competing to raise money for their chosen charities. Armed with £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they are paired with expert thrifters, husband and husband Tom and Terry, and sent out across Chepstow’s charity shops in search of hidden gems that can be turned into profit.
Ella opts for a cautious but considered approach, hunting for quality homeware, collectibles and classic fashion pieces with reliable resale appeal. Early finds boost her confidence, including elegant glassware and vintage decorative items that promise steady returns. Issy, meanwhile, embraces a bolder strategy, gravitating towards statement furniture and eye-catching fashion – pieces that could either soar at auction or fall flat.
As the clock ticks down, tensions rise. A risky spend threatens to blow the budget, and both teams face tough calls about when to stop browsing and commit. Joanna keeps the pressure on, reminding them that hesitation can be just as costly as a bad buy.
Each contestant then chooses one item to be transformed. Rachel’s understated furniture find is refreshed into a stylish, contemporary piece, while Cerys’s more daring choice is given a dramatic makeover by a specialist upcycler, elevating it from charity shop cast-off to standout showpiece.
The episode builds to a live-streamed auction, where Ella and Issy must sell their collections to an online audience in real time. Nerves are high as bids come in thick and fast, and the balance of power shifts repeatedly. Strong storytelling and confident pitching prove crucial, while one surprise result sends shock waves through the competition.
When the final figures are revealed, there is a clear winner on the scoreboard. But the real triumph is the money raised for charity, proving once again that second-hand shopping can deliver real-world impact.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the elegant spa town of Harrogate, the gateway to the Yorkshire Dales, for a high-stakes thrifting showdown.
Today’s competitors are best friends – and former Traitors stars – Sonja and Aubrey, swapping the round table for the rails as they compete to raise money for a local cat sanctuary in Nottinghamshire. With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they split up with expert thrifters Jen and Mirain to tackle Harrogate’s 17 charity shops.
Sonja adopts a disciplined approach, focusing on timeless, high-quality fabrics and classic tailoring. She quickly snaps up a Viyella dress and a Harris Tweed jacket woven from 100 per cent Scottish wool – pieces she believes will always have an audience. But her laser focus on craftsmanship means she and Jen unknowingly pass up on Joanna’s pick of the day: a designer Manuel Ritz jacket with serious resale potential.
Across town, Aubrey leans into bold style and personality. His eye is drawn to standout 1980s fashion, including a pair of Paloma Picasso shoes that ooze retro glamour. However, Joanna worries he may be falling into a common thrifting trap – choosing pieces he loves personally rather than thinking purely about profit.
As time ticks away, attention turns to the all-important upcycling challenge. Aubrey takes a creative risk, pairing a floral embroidered tablecloth with a plain white shirt in the hope of creating a bespoke fashion statement. Meanwhile, Sonja opts for drama, gambling on a heavy Egyptian-style tapestry that could be transformed into a striking new piece.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must step into the spotlight as sellers. Aubrey’s natural charisma shines as he models his reworked creation, injecting energy and humour into the room. Sonja counters with calm authority, drawing on her knowledge of fabrics and tailoring to build bidder confidence.
When live sales are combined with a week of online trading, it’s an incredibly tight finish – proof that strategy, style and salesmanship all count in equal measure. But beyond the friendly rivalry, the real winner is Aubrey and Sonja's chosen charity, with a substantial total raised thanks to a fast-paced day of Yorkshire thrifting.
